business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Himalaya Nutravedics India Limited manufactures, markets and distributes Ayurvedic formulations and nutraceutical products in India and undertakes third-party contract manufacturing for similar companies. Its portfolio spans classical (Shastric) Ayurvedic formulations, proprietary Ayurvedic products and nutraceutical supplements across softgel and hardgel capsules, tablets, liquid orals, medicated oils and protein powders, covering gut health, immunity, metabolic health, musculoskeletal and joint wellness, reproductive vitality, respiratory wellness, pain management and general wellness. Products are sold to healthcare practitioners, stockists, distributors and retailers through a doctor-centric, field-force driven pan-India network, and to third-party manufacturing customers.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Softgel Capsules:** Ayurvedic and Nutraceutical softgel capsule formulations made by encapsulation of oil/ghee-based and extract-based ingredients, including classical Ayurvedic compositions and proprietary formulations, FY2026 revenue ₹2,572.61 lakhs (59.73% of revenue from operations); FY2025 ₹1,226.90 lakhs (58.43%); FY2024 ₹938.99 lakhs (65.09%)
- **Medicated Oils:** Medicated Ayurvedic oils formulated using classical Ayurvedic processing methods such as Taila paka vidhi and Sneha paka vidhi, intended for external application (massage applications, general body care), FY2026 revenue ₹1,289.14 lakhs (29.93%); FY2025 ₹565.60 lakhs (26.94%); FY2024 ₹46.97 lakhs (3.26%)
- **Tablets:** Ayurvedic and Nutraceutical tablet formulations made using standardized blending and compression processes, from herbal extracts, mineral ingredients and plant-based actives, FY2026 revenue ₹331.16 lakhs (7.69%); FY2025 ₹125.42 lakhs (5.97%); FY2024 ₹208.40 lakhs (14.45%)
- **Others (Liquid orals, Hardgel capsules, Protein powders):** Hardgel capsules, protein powders and liquid orals for general wellness, nutritional supplementation and lifestyle-related wellness segments, FY2026 revenue ₹113.84 lakhs (2.64%); FY2025 ₹181.72 lakhs (8.65%); FY2024 ₹248.20 lakhs (17.21%)

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward: the Company operates an integrated in-house manufacturing facility capable of producing medicated oils, soft gelatin capsules, hard gelatin capsules, tablets and liquid orals, which the DRHP states allows it to develop, scale and commercialise products across multiple formats "without reliance on external manufacturers". Raw materials are procured exclusively from approved and qualified vendors: herbal raw materials from approved suppliers, contract farming units and certified collectors (whole dried herbs, coarse cuts or fine powders); herbal extracts from GMP-certified manufacturers or authorized contract extraction facilities with documentation on extraction ratios, marker compounds and residual solvent limits; medicated oils either sourced from GMP-approved manufacturers or processed in-house from base oils such as sesame, coconut, castor or olive oil; vitamins, minerals and excipients from pharmaceutical- or nutraceutical-grade suppliers compliant with USP, BP, EP or FCC. Incoming materials are quarantined under "Under Test" labelling, tested by the Quality Control department (identification, organoleptic evaluation, loss on drying, assay, microbial limits, heavy metals, pesticide residues, acid value, peroxide value) and stored on FIFO/FEFO principles with full traceability documentation (vendor qualification records, CoA, QC reports, inventory logs). There are no long-term agreements with suppliers, and the top 1 supplier accounted for 62.13% of total purchases in Fiscal 2026. Forward: finished goods are stored in inventory and distributed to stockists, distributors and retailers through the Company's own sales and distribution network of more than 60 distributors, supported by carrying and forwarding agents and an in-house field force / medical representative organisation; the Company operates a hybrid model balancing its own branded products with third-party contract manufacturing to optimise capacity utilisation and revenue stability, and states a strategic intent to progressively increase the share of own-brand revenue while retaining third-party manufacturing selectively to support capacity utilisation.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Hybrid business model deliberately balances own branded products against third-party contract manufacturing to optimise capacity utilisation and revenue stability
- Mix shift toward own-brand products is the stated margin lever — branded sales contribute approximately 50-52% of revenues against approximately 48-50% from third-party manufacturing, and management intends to raise the branded share
- Product mix has swung sharply toward medicated oils (3.26% of revenue in FY2024 to 26.94% in FY2025 to 29.93% in FY2026) while softgel capsules remain the largest category at 59.73% in FY2026
- Operating leverage on a largely under-utilised single-shift asset base — EBITDA margin moved from 6.48% (FY2024) to 14.24% (FY2025) to 18.82% (FY2026) as revenue from operations scaled from ₹1,442.56 lakhs to ₹4,306.75 lakhs
- Doctor-centric detailing rather than mass-media advertising keeps marketing spend targeted; a uniform national maximum retail price is followed, with margins varying by state and product, and a 2% cash discount is extended for payments received within 14 days
- Working capital is the dominant funding need — a stated working capital requirement of up to ₹3,267.97 lakhs, of which up to ₹1,375.00 lakhs is to come from issue proceeds and up to ₹1,892.97 lakhs from internal accruals or borrowings
- Leverage has fallen materially, with the debt to equity ratio moving from 2.39 times in FY2024 to 0.26 times in FY2025 and 0.31 times in FY2026
- Raw material sourcing is concentrated — the top supplier accounted for 62.13% of total purchases and the top 10 for 94.30% in FY2026 — with all materials procured from approved and qualified vendors under quarantine, testing and FIFO/FEFO controls

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expansion of the branded products business on a pan-India basis — expanding the geographic footprint and deepening penetration beyond the 17 states covered as of March 31, 2026, continuing to expand the field force, and appointing and periodically rotating stockists in strategically identified territories, supported by a doctor-centric engagement model of scientific detailing, CME programmes, medical camps and BFD camps
- Expansion and diversification of the product portfolio — launching an optimal number of new classical Ayurvedic, proprietary Ayurvedic and nutraceutical formulations annually across cardiac and metabolic wellness, diabetes management, pain management, gut health, infertility, immunity, women wellness and general wellness, and strengthening over-the-counter (OTC) offerings to address retail channel demand
- Increasing contribution from higher-margin sales — progressively raising the share of own-brand products in overall revenues while reducing relative dependence on third-party manufacturing, which will continue selectively to support capacity utilisation
- Manufacturing and operational strengthening — optimising procurement cycles, strengthening vendor management, and refining logistics and inventory management systems to handle multi-SKU production and distribution cycles, also building readiness for potential export activities
- Entry into export markets — exploring export opportunities in selected international markets including Africa, the Middle East, Southeast Asia and CIS regions, in a calibrated manner and without reliance on exports as a primary revenue source in the near term
- Digital outreach and market development — deploying a portion of the Net Proceeds towards performance marketing campaigns, search engine optimisation and strategic collaborations across online platforms, and increasing presence across the website, social media platforms and online marketplaces

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The DRHP describes no new plant, brownfield line or greenfield capacity addition. Growth is to come from the existing single leased integrated facility at IDA Cherlapally, Hyderabad, whose installed capacity is computed on a one-shift (8-hour), 25-working-days-per-month basis while the factory has the capability to operate up to three shifts per calendar day — leaving substantial latent headroom, reinforced by FY2025-26 utilisation of only 17.84% on tablets, 13.00% on liquid orals, 10.87% on protein powder and 4.25% on hardgel capsules, against 63.72% on softgel capsules and 90.20% on medicated oil. Expansion is therefore commercial rather than physical: widening the branded footprint beyond the 17 states covered as of March 31, 2026 through more field-force personnel and stockists, broadening the third-party manufacturing client base beyond Kerala, launching new formulations and OTC products, building brand and digital presence with issue proceeds, and calibrated entry into export markets in Africa, the Middle East, Southeast Asia and CIS regions.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated multi-dosage manufacturing capability — one facility able to manufacture medicated oils, soft gelatin capsules, hard gelatin capsules, tablets and liquid orals, allowing products to be developed, scaled and commercialised across formats without reliance on external manufacturers and supporting faster launches
- Doctor acceptance supported by product performance rather than mass advertising — repeat prescriptions and re-ordering by healthcare practitioners achieved through scientific detailing, continuing medical education programmes, medical camps and practitioner engagement, which also keeps marketing costs controlled
- Long-standing relationships with suppliers and customers — repeat orders from practitioners and stockists on the branded side and recurring multi-cycle engagement from third-party manufacturing customers
- Geographic expansion achieved over a relatively short operating history — presence across multiple states within approximately three years of initiating offline sales and marketing operations, having commenced business operations in September 2022
- Broad therapeutic coverage across Ayurvedic and nutraceutical segments — gut health, cardiac and metabolic wellness, diabetes management, pain management, immunity, infertility and general wellness — enabling cross-selling across therapeutic areas
- In-house quality systems evidenced by WHO-GMP, AYUSH GMP, ISO 22000:2018, ISO 9001:2015, HACCP, HALAL and KOSHER certifications, supporting both branded and contract-manufacturing customers

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer concentration — The single largest customer accounted for ₹1,551.50 lakhs, or 36.02% of FY2026 revenue from operations (49.54% in FY2025, 43.02% in FY2024); the top 3 accounted for 56.33%, the top 5 for 65.61% and the top 10 for 81.24%. Loss of one large account would materially dent revenue.
- Supplier concentration — The DRHP carries a risk factor titled 'We have historically derived, and may continue to derive, a significant portion of our supply from top 10 Suppliers'. The top supplier represented ₹1,969.08 lakhs or 62.13% of total purchases in FY2026 and the top 10 represented 94.30%, notwithstanding the Company's stated position that it is not dependent on any single vendor.
- Regional concentration of revenue and of the third-party manufacturing segment — Kerala alone contributed ₹2,124.72 lakhs, 49.33% of FY2026 revenue (68.92% in FY2025), and third-party manufacturing operations are primarily concentrated in Kerala, which contributes approximately 90% of that segment's revenue. Management states it continuously evaluates opportunities to broaden the geographic spread to mitigate regional concentration risk.
- Single-site manufacturing on leased premises — All production runs from one leased integrated facility of approximately 12,544 square feet at IDA Cherlapally, Hyderabad. Any disruption, loss of tenancy or regulatory action at that single site would halt output across every dosage form.
- Dependence on third-party contract manufacturing revenue — Approximately 48-50% of revenues come from third-party manufacturing arrangements, a stream management itself intends to de-emphasise in favour of higher-margin own-brand sales; the transition exposes revenue continuity if branded growth does not replace contract volumes.
- Low capacity utilisation across most dosage forms — On the annualised single-shift basis, FY2025-26 utilisation was 17.84% for tablets, 13.00% for liquid orals, 10.87% for protein powder and 4.25% for hardgel capsules; only softgel capsules (63.72%) and medicated oil (90.20%) run at scale, so a material part of the installed asset base is idle and carries fixed cost.
- Working capital intensity — A stated working capital requirement of up to ₹3,267.97 lakhs against FY2026 revenue from operations of ₹4,306.75 lakhs, of which up to ₹1,892.97 lakhs must still be met from internal accruals or borrowings even after applying up to ₹1,375.00 lakhs of issue proceeds.
- Short operating history — The Company was incorporated on June 16, 2022 and commenced business the same day, converting to a public limited company only in December 2025; the FY2024-FY2026 record on which the issue rests covers barely three years of trading.
